sentences.text: The name Paraplacodus means "Almost Placodus" because the animal resembles Placodus, a large, scaly, tooth-filled newt-like creature.
This small reptile measured about 1.5 meters in total body length.
Fossils of Paraplacodus were found in Northern Italy and the species was named by Bernhard Peyer in 1931.
Specialized anterior teeth suggest that Paraplacodus fed on small, raspberry-shaped macroalgae.
Paraplacodus broilii is an extinct placodont sauropterygian that lived from the Anisian to the Ladinian stages of the Middle Triassic.
The animal belongs to the kingdom Animalia, phylum Chordata, class Sauropsida, superorder Sauropterygia, order Placodontia, family Paraplacodontidae, and genus Paraplacodus.
Paraplacodus lived during the Middle Triassic period.
